english.title: Make an acquisition in contravention of a warning / decision / final notice
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), made an acquisition of **(..SPECIFY THE THING ACQUIRED..) in contravention of a

(A)_[warning notice given under section 189(4)(b)(ii)]_
(B)_[decision notice given under section 189(7)]_
(C)_[final notice which confirmed a decision notice under section 189]_

of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000
english.legislation: Contrary to section 191F(4) and (9) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

english.notes:
(i) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) For the purpose of this offence, the appropriate regulator means -
(a) where the UK authorised person is a PRA-authorised person, the Prudential Regulation Authority;
(b) in any other case, the Financial Conduct Authority.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
